frame_4a219453a9c3.question: Vulnerability analysis of DegenBox
artifact_refs: Share-based balance and elastic total accounting
Strategy profit and loss updates
Withdrawal authorization and share-to-amount conversion
Share transfers and flash-loan callback invariants
Reentrancy and post-operation balance checks

history.rationale: WHY NOW: DegenBox is foundational custody and accounting infrastructure used by lending and liquidity components, and its strategy-adjusted elastic totals plus withdrawal authorization create high-impact opportunities for balance inflation, unauthorized withdrawals, or insolvency. EXIT CRITERIA: Trace every state transition affecting user shares, token totals, strategy balances, and approvals; verify authorization, rounding, callback ordering, reentrancy protections, and flash-loan repayment invariants; conclude with either concrete exploitability evidence or documented proof that these invariants hold across deposit, transfer, withdrawal, and strategy-loss/profit paths.

frame_dc043ef56902.question: Vulnerability analysis of Cauldron borrow, collateral, accrual and exchange-rate state
artifact_refs: Borrow and collateral accounting invariants
Accrued interest and total debt state transitions
Exchange-rate caching and stale-state effects
Share-to-amount conversions and rounding
Consistency between storage state and liquidation or solvency checks

history.rationale: WHY NOW: This unvisited component holds the protocol’s core lending state and is directly connected to the existing high-confidence oracle_failure hypothesis, so stale or inconsistently updated values could amplify insolvency or enable under-collateralized borrowing. It also has critical accounting invariants that have not yet been covered despite Cauldron contract logic being visited. EXIT CRITERIA: Trace every write and read of borrow, collateral, accrual, total-debt, and exchange-rate state; establish the expected invariants across borrow, repay, accrue, liquidation, and solvency paths; and document any exploitable mismatch, stale-value acceptance, precision loss, or confirm that no such state-level vulnerability exists.

frame_e4104de556c7.question: Vulnerability analysis of LockingMultiRewards
artifact_refs: Reward accrual and distribution accounting across multiple reward tokens
Stake locking, boost calculations, and withdrawal timing
StakeFor integration and authorization boundaries
Owner-controlled reward token setup and staking-token excess recovery
Rounding, underfunded rewards, and state-update ordering

history.rationale: WHY NOW: This is an unvisited major component with complex multi-token accounting and lock-based authorization, creating elevated risk of reward inflation, premature withdrawal, permanent fund locking, or privileged asset extraction. EXIT CRITERIA: Trace every external and administrative state transition, verify reward indexes and user balances across stake, withdraw, claim, and reward-notification paths, confirm lock and boost invariants, and determine whether any unauthorized caller can alter accounting or recover user funds. Conclude with either a concrete vulnerability hypothesis or documented evidence that these invariants hold.

frame_090d1470b969.question: Vulnerability analysis of BlastPoints
artifact_refs: External configuration calls and hardcoded target addresses
Operator authorization and configuration trust boundaries
Parameter validation and failure handling
Whether points configuration can redirect, misaccount, or lock protocol rewards

history.rationale: WHY NOW: BlastPoints is an unvisited library that performs external configuration through a hardcoded target and unconditionally configures an operator, creating a high-value permission and integration boundary not covered by the completed Cauldron, DegenBox, or rewards investigations. EXIT CRITERIA: Trace every BlastPoints call site and configuration parameter, verify target and operator invariants, confirm authorization and failure semantics, and determine whether any reachable path permits unauthorized configuration, denial of service, or misdirected points; conclude with no issue if all invariants are enforced.

frame_0e8ce7ec25c9.question: Vulnerability analysis of BlastTokenRegistry
artifact_refs: Owner-controlled token-to-configuration mapping updates
Authorization and validation of registry writes, including zero or malformed token addresses
Downstream consumers relying on registry entries for token claims or yield handling
Ability to overwrite, disable, or redirect registered token behavior

history.rationale: WHY NOW: BlastTokenRegistry is an unvisited permissioned component and its owner-controlled mappings may gate token claims across Blast-specific contracts, making registry corruption or unauthorized updates security-relevant. EXIT CRITERIA: Trace every registry read and write, verify caller authorization and input validation, determine whether entries can be maliciously replaced or disabled, and establish whether any resulting impact is limited to administrative configuration or can redirect funds or block claims.

frame_d8652d888bee.question: Vulnerability analysis of BlastYields
artifact_refs: Yield accrual and claim calculations
Interactions with Blast yield precompiles or external token contracts
Recipient and authorization handling
Behavior on unsupported tokens, failed calls, and zero balances
Accounting consistency across yield modes

history.rationale: WHY NOW: BlastYields is the only identified unvisited non-interface component and directly supports yield handling across Blast-integrated contracts, making it a critical remaining coverage gap with potential external-call and accounting risks. EXIT CRITERIA: Trace every public and internal library operation through all callers; verify authorization, recipient selection, yield-mode assumptions, external-call failure handling, and accounting invariants; document any exploitable issue or conclude that no vulnerability is supported by static analysis.

frame_83db53548465.question: Vulnerability analysis of MasterContractManager
artifact_refs: Master contract registration and whitelist administration
Signed user approval validation, replay protection, and domain separation
Ownership and authorization boundaries for clone deployment or protocol integration
State transitions affecting approved master contracts

history.rationale: WHY NOW: MasterContractManager is an uncompleted, permission-critical component that controls which master contracts can participate in the protocol and processes signed user approvals, creating high-impact risks from authorization bypasses, signature replay, or improperly scoped administrative control. EXIT CRITERIA: Trace every registration, whitelist, approval, and deployment-related state transition; verify caller authorization, signature domain/nonce handling, replay resistance, zero-address and replacement behavior, and downstream enforcement, then document any exploitable path or conclude that these controls are sound.
